uncertain_diagram_candidates.title: 3SAT polynomial-time many-one reduces to directed Hamiltonian cycle
exact_claims: Line 61 defines each variable gadget X_i as the bidirected crossbar s_{i,0} ↔ ℓ_{i,1} ↔ r_{i,1} ↔ s_{i,1} ↔ … ↔ s_{i,m}, adds p_i→s_{i,0}, p_i→s_{i,m}, s_{i,0}→q_i, s_{i,m}→q_i, identifies q_i=p_{i+1}, and adds literal detours ℓ_{i,j}→c_j→r_{i,j} for x_i and r_{i,j}→c_j→ℓ_{i,j} for ¬x_i.

Lines 63–65 claim that the two crossbar orientations encode true/false and that each clause vertex is visited by a same-pair detour exactly when a selected literal is true; the converse excludes other Hamiltonian path shapes.
Lines 67–69 close the sφ-to-tφ path with fresh zφ and arcs zφ→sφ, tφ→zφ.
uncertain_diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The proof relies on the orientation of a repeated crossbar and on clause vertices inserted as detours at particular literal pairs. A small indexed schematic can make the occurrence-to-arc map and forward/reverse route interpretation easier to inspect; it should be a schematic rather than a full graph whose size depends on n,m.
uncertain_diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Show one variable gadget with ordered crossbar vertices s_{i,j-1}, ℓ_{i,j}, r_{i,j}, s_{i,j}; indicate the bidirected crossbar edges, the p_i/q_i boundary arcs, the positive-literal detour ℓ_{i,j}→c_j→r_{i,j}, and the negative-literal detour r_{i,j}→c_j→ℓ_{i,j}. Mark left-to-right as x_i=true and right-to-left as x_i=false. If including the cycle conversion, separately show zφ→sφ and tφ→zφ. Verify occurrence indices and all arrow orientations against source lines 61–67.
uncertain_diagram_candidates.note: The source prose already specifies the construction and proof. This is optional visual support, not a confirmed mathematical defect or a requirement to add a diagram.
